subject.title: WhatsApp 1:1: inbound image wedges main lane ~3min before processing — multimodal run strands active_reply_work/queued_work_without_active_run (repro on 2026.6.10, post-#95039)

question: Should WhatsApp direct-image active_reply_work after terminal multimodal progress be fixed as its own session-owner cleanup path, or folded under the broader WhatsApp durable replay and owner-lock tracker?
rationale: Current source and reporter logs support a real lane-stall family, but the safest fix depends on maintainer intent for active-work liveness versus faster terminal-progress release, and the open canonical PR only covers part of the overlap.

options.title: Keep focused and require live proof
options.body: Keep this issue open as the direct-image multimodal variant until a current-main WhatsApp repro proves whether active_reply_work still loops independently of durable replay.

options.title: Fold into canonical tracker
options.body: Treat this as evidence for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97538 if maintainers decide the direct-image loop is the same owner-lock failure and should be tracked only there.

options.title: Close after current-main proof
options.body: Close as implemented only if a live current-main run or targeted regression proves the image burst drains without repeated released=0 abort cycles.

recommendation.title: Keep focused and require live proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the direct-image multimodal variant until a current-main WhatsApp repro proves whether active_reply_work still loops independently of durable replay.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent recovery commits are closest to the released=0 session-lane reset behavior that must be evaluated before changing policy.
